display_name: Stand a gauge canary down, ledger and registry both
description: GAU-24 (2026-08-19). Closes a leak measured across every prior canary exercise: the registry mark was retirable (retire_canary, the store primitive) but wired to no verb, and the ledger row was stuck a second, independent way -- retire_session refused a canary row with unsupported_on_host because host 'synthetic' had no host driver. Every exercise therefore left one active canary mark plus one permanently-'live' managed_session row that nothing could retire, standing debt that accumulates per exercise rather than a one-time cost. This verb closes both halves. It registers a no-op 'synthetic' host driver (spawn and terminate both refuse loudly, exactly like the existing degenerate 'operator' driver for a row nothing ever spawned) so retire_session can reach the ledger row, then composes two acts in a fixed, ledger-first order: if a managed_session row exists for this identity, retire_session runs first; only once that succeeds, or there was never a row to retire, does the registry mark get stamped retired_at. That order is deliberate -- it makes the registry mark mean 'this canary's lifecycle is actually finished' rather than merely 'someone asked to retire it.' If the ledger step fails, the registry mark is left untouched, so the canary stays honestly active rather than recording a retirement that never happened. If the ledger step succeeds and the registry-mark write then fails, the result is safely re-drivable: retire_session is idempotent on an already-retired row, and the registry-mark write is an idempotent predicated update, so re-running this verb finishes the job rather than wedging it. The fail-closed distinction this depends on is narrow and deliberate: only the literal, explicitly-declared host name 'synthetic' resolves to the no-op driver -- a host name that genuinely has no driver registered in this build still raises unsupported_on_host, exactly as before this fix, so a real orphaned session on an unresolvable host is never mistaken for a canary and marked retirable without anything being torn down.
embedding_description: Tearing down a deliberately fake monitoring-test session all the way -- both its fleet ledger entry and its registry mark -- so running the tamper-test exercise repeatedly stops leaving permanent fake sessions behind that nothing can clean up and that eventually show up as false overdue-session alarms.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: agent_instance_id, session_row_existed (whether a managed_session row was found and retired), session_retire_result (retire_session's own outcome when a row existed, else null), canary_mark_retired (always true on success).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: State plainly whether a ledger row existed and was retired, or the canary had only ever been registered. Do not imply the canary can still be re-armed without re-registering -- retiring stands it down for good, on the record.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: A retired canary is no longer active (is_active_canary is now false) and drops out of the operational canary filter list, but stays visible with include_retired=true for anyone reading back its old alarms.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: One registry read, then (conditionally) the full retire_session sequence -- terminate through the no-op synthetic host driver, dependency-edge firing, role-claim cleanup, and a predicated terminated-to-retired transition -- and finally the registry mark's predicated update, all through the state interface.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: not_a_canary: this identity is not a registered canary at all, so there is nothing to retire. Any error code retire_session itself can raise (e.g. unsupported_on_host, illegal_lifecycle_transition, stale_lifecycle_state) surfaces unchanged if the ledger step fails -- the registry mark is left untouched in that case. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For not_a_canary, confirm the identity was registered with register_gauge_canary before retrying. For an error surfaced from the composed retire_session step, resolve it the same way you would a bare retire_session failure, then re-run this verb -- both halves are safe to repeat.
